objectives.title: Define the benefits of the AWS Cloud
objectives.summary: Trade capital expense (CapEx) for variable expense (OpEx), economies of scale, elasticity, agility, global reach, and stop guessing capacity.
objectives.notes_md:
**Six Advantages of Cloud Computing:**
- `Trade CapEx for OpEx` — pay only when you consume computing resources.
- `Benefit from massive economies of scale` — lower pay-as-you-go prices from aggregate usage.
- `Stop guessing capacity` — scale up or down on demand instead of over-provisioning.
- `Increase speed and agility` — provision resources in minutes.
- `Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers` — focus on applications and customers.
- `Go global in minutes` — deploy across AWS Regions and Edge Locations worldwide.

objectives.title: Identify design principles of the AWS Well-Architected Framework
objectives.summary: Six pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability.
objectives.notes_md:
**Six Pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework:**
- `Operational Excellence` — run and monitor systems, perform operations as code, make frequent small reversible changes.
- `Security` — protect data/systems, apply least privilege, enable traceability, automate security best practices.
- `Reliability` — recover from infrastructure/service disruptions, dynamically acquire compute resources, mitigate single points of failure across Multi-AZ.
- `Performance Efficiency` — use computing resources efficiently, go serverless, democratize advanced technologies.
- `Cost Optimization` — avoid unnecessary cost, adopt consumption models, measure efficiency.
- `Sustainability` — minimize environmental impacts of running cloud workloads.

objectives.title: Understand cloud migration and the AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)
objectives.summary: Six CAF perspectives (Business, People, Governance, Platform, Security, Operations) and the 7 Rs of migration.
objectives.notes_md:
**AWS CAF Perspectives:**
- *Business capabilities*: `Business` · `People` · `Governance`
- *Technical capabilities*: `Platform` · `Security` · `Operations`

**Common Migration Strategies (7 Rs):**
- `Rehost` (lift-and-shift) · `Relocate` (hypervisor-level move) · `Replatform` (lift-tinker-and-shift) · `Refactor` (re-architect to cloud-native) · `Repurchase` (move to SaaS) · `Retain` · `Retire`.

objectives.title: Understand the AWS Shared Responsibility Model
objectives.summary: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud; the customer is responsible for security IN the cloud.
objectives.notes_md:
**Shared Responsibility Breakdown:**
- `AWS (Security OF the Cloud)` — physical data centers, hardware, global network, hypervisor, and managed service infrastructure.
- `Customer (Security IN the Cloud)` — customer data, IAM users/roles/policies, OS patching on EC2, network/firewall configuration (Security Groups, NACLs), client-side/server-side encryption.
- Responsibility shifts by service model: `IaaS` (EC2) gives customer more OS/network control; `PaaS`/`Abstracted` (RDS, Lambda, S3) shifts OS and platform patching to AWS.

objectives.title: Understand AWS Cloud security, governance, and compliance concepts
objectives.summary: AWS Artifact, AWS Config, AWS CloudTrail, Amazon Inspector, Amazon GuardDuty, AWS Shield, and AWS WAF.
objectives.notes_md:
**Compliance & Threat Detection Services:**
- `AWS Artifact` — on-demand access to AWS compliance reports (SOC, PCI, ISO) and agreements (BAA).
- `AWS CloudTrail` — audits API calls and account activity across AWS.
- `AWS Config` — tracks resource configuration history and evaluates compliance against rules.
- `Amazon GuardDuty` — intelligent threat detection analyzing VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and CloudTrail events.
- `Amazon Inspector` — automated vulnerability scanning for EC2, ECR container images, and Lambda functions.
- `AWS Shield` — managed DDoS protection (`Shield Standard` is automatic/free; `Shield Advanced` offers 24/7 SRT & cost protection).
- `AWS WAF` — web application firewall protecting against SQL injection and XSS at CloudFront/ALB/API Gateway.

objectives.title: Identify AWS access management capabilities
objectives.summary: IAM users, groups, roles, policies, MFA, AWS IAM Identity Center (SSO), and AWS KMS.
objectives.notes_md:
**Identity and Access Management (IAM):**
- `Root user` — lock away access keys, enable MFA immediately, use only for account-level tasks.
- `IAM Roles` — temporary security credentials via AWS STS; preferred for EC2 instances, Lambda functions, and cross-account access.
- `IAM Policies` — JSON documents defining explicit `Allow` or `Deny` permissions; explicit `Deny` always overrides `Allow`.
- `AWS IAM Identity Center` — centralized workforce single sign-on across multiple AWS accounts.
- `AWS KMS` — managed cryptographic keys for encryption at rest across AWS services.

objectives.title: Identify AWS Global Infrastructure and networking services
objectives.summary: Regions, Availability Zones, Edge Locations, Amazon VPC, Subnets, Security Groups, NACLs, Route 53, CloudFront, Direct Connect.
objectives.notes_md:
**Global Infrastructure:**
- `Region` — physical geographic area containing 3+ isolated `Availability Zones (AZs)`.
- `Availability Zone` — one or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity.
- `Edge Locations` — used by `Amazon CloudFront` (CDN) and `Amazon Route 53` (DNS) to cache content and route traffic with low latency.

**Networking:**
- `Security Group` — stateful instance-level virtual firewall (allow rules only).
- `Network ACL (NACL)` — stateless subnet-level firewall (supports allow and deny rules).
- `AWS Direct Connect` — dedicated private fiber connection from on-premises to AWS (bypasses public internet).

objectives.title: Identify AWS compute and serverless services
objectives.summary: Amazon EC2, Auto Scaling, Elastic Load Balancing, AWS Lambda, Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS, AWS Fargate, Elastic Beanstalk.
objectives.notes_md:
**Compute Options:**
- `Amazon EC2` — customizable virtual servers in the cloud.
- `AWS Lambda` — serverless, event-driven compute; pay only for compute time consumed (up to 15-minute execution).
- `Amazon ECS / Amazon EKS` — container orchestration for Docker and Kubernetes.
- `AWS Fargate` — serverless compute engine for containers (works with ECS and EKS).
- `AWS Elastic Beanstalk` — PaaS service where developers upload code and Beanstalk handles provisioning, load balancing, scaling, and monitoring.

objectives.title: Identify AWS storage and database services
objectives.summary: Amazon S3, EBS, EFS, Storage Gateway, RDS, Aurora, DynamoDB, ElastiCache, Redshift.
objectives.notes_md:
**Storage:**
- `Amazon S3` — durable (11 9s) object storage (`S3 Standard`, `S3 Intelligent-Tiering`, `S3 Glacier`).
- `Amazon EBS` — block-level storage volumes attached to EC2 within a single AZ.
- `Amazon EFS` — managed elastic NFS file system shared across multiple EC2 instances and AZs.

**Databases:**
- `Amazon RDS` — managed relational DB (PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server).
- `Amazon Aurora` — AWS-engineered MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible relational DB with 6-way replication across 3 AZs.
- `Amazon DynamoDB` — serverless key-value and document NoSQL database with single-digit millisecond latency.
- `Amazon Redshift` — petabyte-scale data warehouse for OLAP analytics.

objectives.title: Compare AWS pricing models and cost management tools
objectives.summary: On-Demand, Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, Spot Instances, Dedicated Hosts; AWS Budgets, Cost Explorer, Pricing Calculator.
objectives.notes_md:
**EC2 Purchasing Options:**
- `On-Demand` — pay by the second/hour, no long-term commitment; best for spiky/unpredictable workloads.
- `Savings Plans / Reserved Instances (RIs)` — 1-year or 3-year commitment for up to 72% discount on steady-state usage.
- `Spot Instances` — up to 90% discount using spare EC2 capacity; can be interrupted with a 2-minute warning (ideal for fault-tolerant batch jobs).
- `Dedicated Hosts` — physical server dedicated to your use for bring-your-own-license (BYOL) and strict compliance.

**Cost Tools:**
- `AWS Pricing Calculator` — estimate workload cost *before* building.
- `AWS Cost Explorer` — visualize, understand, and forecast historical/future AWS spend.
- `AWS Budgets` — set custom cost/usage budgets and receive SNS/email alerts when thresholds are exceeded.

objectives.title: Understand AWS Organizations and AWS Support plans
objectives.summary: Consolidated billing, Service Control Policies (SCPs), and Basic, Developer, Business, Enterprise On-Ramp, and Enterprise Support.
objectives.notes_md:
**AWS Organizations:**
- Centralizes management of multiple AWS accounts, enables `Consolidated Billing` (volume discounts + single bill), and enforces `Service Control Policies (SCPs)` as permission guardrails.

**AWS Support Tiers:**
- `Basic` — free; 24/7 customer service, documentation, core Trusted Advisor checks.
- `Developer` — business-hours email access to Cloud Support Associates; general guidance.
- `Business` — 24/7 phone/email/chat to Cloud Support Engineers, full `AWS Trusted Advisor` checks, `<1 hour` response for production system down.
- `Enterprise On-Ramp` — pool of Technical Account Managers (TAMs), `<30 min` business-critical response.
- `Enterprise` — designated `Technical Account Manager (TAM)`, `<15 min` response for business-critical system down.
